#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -n 16
#   -N 1
#   -t 0-08:00
#   -p shared
#   --mem-per-cpu 512
#   --open-mode=append
#   -o logs/dsmc_job_%j.out
#   -e logs/dsmc_job_%j.err

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 16
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=8h

# Omitted Slurm option: -p shared (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu 512
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --open-mode=append and -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) and open-mode semantics are not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames; append behavior may not be preserved.

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads

# SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE is not set under Flux; match the requested task count.
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=16

echo "running...."

# Launch 16 ranks under Flux (equivalent to srun -n 16 ...)
flux run -n 16 -c 1 julia RunCells.jl -l 0.002 -L 0.02

reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu 512`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`-p shared`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition constraint; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -n 16 # Number of cores requested
#SBATCH -N 1 # Ensure that all cores are on one machine
#SBATCH -t 0-08:00 # Runtime in minutes
#SBATCH -p shared # Partition to submit to
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu 512 # Memory per cpu in MB (see also ?mem-per-cpu)
#SBATCH --open-mode=append
#SBATCH -o logs/dsmc_job_%j.out # Standard out goes to this file
#SBATCH -e logs/dsmc_job_%j.err # Standard err goes to this filehostname

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE

echo "running...."

julia RunCells.jl -l 0.002 -L 0.02
